### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | This is APA-publisher-wide policy (not Emotion-specific): generative AI use in drafting is permitted but must be disclosed in the Methods section and cited per APA's software-citation template; AI cannot be listed as an author; authors are fully responsible for verifying AI-generated content. AI-assisted copy editing alone need not be declared. Emotion's own submission-guidelines page (apa.org/pubs/journals/emo/submit) repeats this same publisher-wide text verbatim rather than stating a journal-specific variant, so treat this as APA policy applied to Emotion, not a bespoke Emotion policy. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/resources/publishing-tips/policy-generative-ai |

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Yes, preprints are explicitly permitted; APA's general rule against concurrent multi-journal submission does not bar prior preprint posting, but authors must disclose prior dissemination (e.g. the preprint) in the author note.

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Empirical reports, theoretical articles, meta-analytic literature reviews, comments on published work, and direct replications, across the full range of emotion research: cultural, social, personality/temperament, cognitive, developmental, health, and biological (incl. neuroimaging, animal/molecular) approaches to emotional processes. An active 2026 special-issue push is toward affect-dynamics / ecological-momentary-assessment (EMA) designs linking short- and long-timescale affect fluctuations to mental and physical health outcomes.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** laboratory experiments, field/ecological studies, ecological momentary assessment / intensive longitudinal designs, neuroimaging, animal and molecular mechanism studies, meta-analysis, direct replication

- **experiential.desk_reject_pct**: SciRev lists desk-reject rate as n/a for Emotion; no forum or aggregator disclosed a concrete desk-reject percentage
- **experiential.reviewer_culture**: No first-hand forum post (小木虫, 知乎, Reddit r/AskAcademia, LetPub) contained a substantive account of reviewer tone/culture for Emotion — only structural/scope pages and a single terse SciRev complaint about a late-stage decision reversal, which is too thin to characterize 'culture'
- **experiential.acceptance_note (numeric rejection rate)**: A ~77-80% rejection-rate figure recurs on secondary/AI-generated aggregator pages (Grokipedia) but could not be traced to a primary disclosure (APA, JCR, Scopus) within this search pass, so it was excluded rather than reported as fact
- **ai_policy (journal-specific variant)**: Emotion's own submit page reproduces the APA publisher-wide generative-AI text verbatim; no Emotion-specific addendum (stricter or looser than baseline) was found

**Cross-language checks performed (mandatory per methodology):**
